$comment: THE MONEY RENDERING RULE, as a table three independent implementations must agree on.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (012 / T1211). One rule - `Equivalent.precision` is the MINIMUM number
of fraction digits a money string carries, never the maximum - is implemented three times, in
three languages, in three projects that share no module: `app/utils/money.py::to_money_str`,
`simulator-ui/v2/src/utils/money.ts::formatMoney`, and
`admin-ui/src/utils/decimal.ts::formatDecimalMinScale`. There is no npm workspace and no shared
package between the two UIs, so the duplication cannot be removed cheaply.
The duplication is not cosmetic: it was the MECHANISM of a P1. The backend and the simulator UI
carried the rule correctly while admin-ui quantized to exactly `precision` with ROUND_HALF_UP,
so `0.05` of the shipped HOUR (precision 1) - a value the door accepts and Numeric(20, 8) stores
exactly - was shown to operators as `0.1`. Three private test suites all passed. Nothing in the
tree compared the three copies to each other, so nothing could notice.
This table is that comparison. Each implementation has a test that reads THIS file and asserts
its own output against `expected`, so a copy that drifts fails in its own project, and a case
added here is answered by all three at once:
- tests/unit/test_p012_t1211_money_rendering_conformance.py
- simulator-ui/v2/src/utils/money.conformance.test.ts
- admin-ui/src/utils/decimal.conformance.test.ts
SCOPE. Valid plain decimal strings only. The three implementations deliberately differ on
malformed input (the backend raises on non-finite, admin-ui returns the input unchanged,
simulator-ui renders zero) and those differences are documented at each call site, not here.
Exponent notation is not in the table because it cannot be produced by any of the three.
rule: precision is the minimum number of fraction digits, and never fewer than the value itself needs
